source_text:
Erant ingenia de spiritalibus nequitiae, cum quibus luctatio est nobis, fratres, merito contemplanda, fidei necessaria, ut electi manifestentur, ut reprobi detegantur. Et ideo habent vim et in excogitandis instruendisque erroribus facilitatem, non adeo mirandam quasi difficilem et inexplicabilem, cum de saecularibus quoque scripturis exemplum praesto sit eiusmodi facilitatis. Vides hodie ex Vergilio fabulam in totum aliam componi, materia secundum versus et versibus secundum materiam concinnatis. Denique H(??)sidius Geta Medeam tragoediam ex Vergilio plenissime exsuxit. Meus quidam propinquus ex eodem poÃ«ta inter cetera stili sui otia Pinacem Cebetis explicuit. Homerocentones etiam vocari solent qui de carminibus Homeri propria opera more centenario ex multis hinc inde compositis in unum sarciunt corpus. Et utique fecundior divina litteratura ad facultatem cuiusque materiae. Nec periclitor dicere ipsas quoque scripturas sic esse ex dei voluntate dispositas ut haereticis materias subministrarent, cum legam oportere haereses esse, quae sine scripturis esse non possunt.
Sequetur a quo intellectus interpretetur eorum quae ad haereses faciant? A diabolo scilicet, cuius sunt partes intervertendi veritatem, qui ipsas quoque res sacramentorum divinorum idolorum mysteriis aemulatur. Tingit et ipse quosdam, utique credentes et fideles suos; expositionem delictorum de lavacro repromittit: et si adhuc memini, Mithra signat illic in frontibus milites suos; celebrat et panis oblationem, et imaginem resurrectionis inducit, et sub gladio redimit coronam. Quid, quod et summum pontificem in unius nuptiis statuit? habet et virgines, habet et continentes. Ceterum si Numae Pompilii superstitiones revolvamus, si sacerdotalia officia et insignia et privilegia, si sacrificalia ministeria et instrumenta et vasa ipsorum sacrificiorum ac piaculorum et votorum curiositates consideremus, nonne manifeste diabolus morositatem illam Iudaicae legis imitatus est? Qui ergo ipsas res, de quibus sacramenta Christi administrantur, tam aemulanter adfectavit exprimere in negotiis idololatriae, utique et idem et eodem ingenio gestiit et potuit instrumenta quoque divinarum rerum et sanctorum Christianorum; sensum de sensibus, verba de verbis, parabolas de parabolis, profanae et aemulae fidei attemperare. Et ideo neque a diabolo immissa esse spiritalia nequitiae, ex quibus etiam haereses veniunt, dubitare quis debet, neque ab idololatria distare haereses, cum et auctoris et operis eiusdem sint cuius et idololatria. Deum aut fingunt alium adversus creatorem, aut si unicum creatorem confitentur, aliter eum disserunt quam in vero est. Itaque omne mendacium quod de deo dicunt quodammodo genus est idololatriae.
thought_title: The devil's counterfeits and the source of heresies
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that heresies were predicted and serve to test the faithful, and now explains that the devil, who counterfeits divine rites in idolatry, is the source of the spiritual wickedness from which heresies come.
pass_a_gloss: There were spirits of wickedness in heavenly places, with whom is wrestling for us, brothers, rightly to be contemplated, necessary for faith, so that the elect may be made manifest, so that the reprobate may be uncovered. And therefore they have force and facility in thinking out and instructing errors, not so much to be wondered at as if difficult and inexplicable, since from secular writings also an example is at hand of facility of this kind. You see today from Virgil a story entirely different being composed, the matter according to the verses and the verses according to the matter having been fitted together. Finally Hosidius Geta sucked out most fully a Medea tragedy from Virgil. A certain relative of mine from the same poet among the other leisure works of his pen unfolded the Pinax of Cebes. Homerocentones also are usually called those who from the poems of Homer their own works in the manner of a cento from many things composed here and there stitch together into one body. And certainly the divine literature is more fertile for the capacity of each matter. Nor do I risk saying that the Scriptures themselves were thus arranged by the will of God that they might supply materials to heretics, since I read that heresies must exist, which cannot exist without the Scriptures. It will follow from whom the understanding is interpreted of those things which make for heresies? From the devil of course, whose parts are to pervert the truth, who also emulates the very things of the divine sacraments with the mysteries of idols. He also dips certain ones himself, certainly his believers and faithful ones; he promises an exposition of sins from the washing: and if I still remember, Mithras marks there on the foreheads his soldiers; he also celebrates an offering of bread, and introduces an image of resurrection, and under the sword buys back a crown. What, that he also established a chief pontiff in the marriages of one? he has also virgins, he has also the continent. Moreover if we unroll the superstitions of Numa Pompilius, if we consider the priestly offices and insignia and privileges, if the sacrificial ministries and instruments and vessels of the sacrifices themselves and the curiosities of expiations and vows, has not the devil manifestly imitated that scrupulosity of the Jewish law? Therefore he who so emulously desired to express the very things, by which the sacraments of Christ are administered, in the affairs of idolatry, certainly the same one both with the same genius desired and was able to fit also the instruments of divine things and of holy Christians; sense from senses, words from words, parables from parables, to a profane and emulous faith. And therefore no one ought to doubt either that spiritual wickednesses have been sent in by the devil, from which also heresies come, nor that heresies differ from idolatry, since they are of the same author and work as idolatry. They either fashion another god against the creator, or if they confess the one creator, they discuss him otherwise than he is in truth. And so every falsehood which they say about God is in a certain way a kind of idolatry.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Pauline phrase, keeping the genitive of quality and the adjective 'spiritual' as 'spirits' to match the biblical source.

choices.english: the elect may be made manifest, so that the reprobate may be uncovered
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of both verbs and the parallel purpose clauses; 'uncovered' preserves the literal sense of detegantur.
rejected: the chosen may be revealed, so that the rejected may be exposed
the elect may appear, so that the reprobate may be detected

choices.why: The term is a technical name for cento poems made from Homer; keeping the Latin form preserves the technical sense.
Subministro means to furnish or supply; 'materials' keeps the sense of raw content for heretical use.

choices.english: he promises an exposition of sins from the washing
choices.why: Literal rendering of repromittit as 'promises' and lavacro as 'washing', preserving the baptismal parallel.
rejected: he promises forgiveness of sins from the bath
he promises a declaration of sins from the washing

choices.english: that scrupulosity of the Jewish law
choices.why: Morositas means fussy scrupulosity or fastidiousness; 'scrupulosity' captures the pejorative tone toward Jewish legal observance.
rejected: that fussiness of the Jewish law
that fastidiousness of the Jewish law

bible_refs.note: spiritalibus nequitiae, cum quibus luctatio est nobis

pass_b_english: Brothers, there are spirits of wickedness with whom we wrestle. They deserve our attention, and they are necessary for faith, so that the elect may be made manifest and the reprobate may be uncovered. That is why they have power and facility in devising and constructing errors. This facility is not so remarkable, as if it were difficult and inexplicable, since an example of such facility is ready at hand even from secular writings. You see today how a story is composed from Virgil in a completely different way, with the subject matter fitted to the verses and the verses fitted to the subject matter. In fact, Hosidius Geta drew out a whole tragedy of Medea from Virgil. A relative of mine, among other leisure works of his pen, worked out the Tablet of Cebes from the same poet. People are even called Homer-centonists who stitch together into one body, in the manner of a patchwork, their own works from many passages of Homer's poems gathered here and there. And certainly the divine literature is more fertile for the capacity of any subject matter. Nor do I risk saying that the Scriptures themselves were arranged by God's will so that they might supply materials for heretics, since I read that there must be heresies, which cannot exist without the Scriptures.

It follows: by whom is the understanding of those things that make for heresies interpreted? By the devil, of course, whose part it is to pervert the truth, who also emulates the very realities of the divine sacraments in the mysteries of idols. He too baptizes certain people, his believers and faithful ones, of course. He promises an exposition of sins from the washing. And if I still remember, Mithras marks his soldiers there on their foreheads. He also celebrates an offering of bread, and introduces an image of the resurrection, and under the sword he buys back a crown. What of the fact that he also established a high priest for the marriage of one man? He has virgins too, and he has the continent. Moreover, if we review the superstitions of Numa Pompilius, if we consider the priestly offices and insignia and privileges, the sacrificial ministries and instruments and vessels of the sacrifices themselves, and the curiosities of expiations and vows, is it not clear that the devil imitated that scrupulosity of the Jewish law? Therefore he who so emulously desired to express the very realities by which the sacraments of Christ are administered in the business of idolatry, surely the same one, with the same talent, also desired and was able to adapt the instruments of divine realities and of holy Christians to a profane and rival faith: sense from senses, words from words, parables from parables. And therefore no one should doubt either that the spirits of wickedness, from which heresies also come, were sent by the devil, or that heresies differ from idolatry, since they are of the same author and the same work as idolatry. They either invent another god against the Creator, or if they confess the one Creator, they explain him differently than he is in truth. And so every falsehood they speak about God is in some way a kind of idolatry.
notes: The source text contains 'H(??)sidius Geta' with uncertain characters; the name is Hosidius Geta, a known author of a Medea tragedy composed from Virgil. The gloss renders the name as Hosidius Geta.

last_rejected.quote: worked out the Tablet of Cebes
last_rejected.why: Latin refers to Cebes' painting, not a tablet; the English adds a different work.
last_rejected.ruling: Pinax means tablet/painting/board; 'Tablet of Cebes' is the standard title of the work, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: The source mentions only curiosities of vows, not expiations; 'expiations' is an unwarranted addition.
last_rejected.ruling: Source says 'piaculorum et votorum'; piaculorum = expiations. The English correctly renders both nouns; no addition.

polish.changed: Clarified sentence structure and rhythm for modern readers, made the speaker's voice consistent, and ensured each pronoun and reference is clear while preserving every claim, qualification, and Scripture reference exactly.
